extracted.intended_audience: parties and practitioners in USPTO contested proceedings (applicants, patentees, patent attorneys/agents), and administrative patent judges
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evidentiary rules for contested cases and patent interferences before the USPTO Board, covering filing requirements, motions, discovery, testimony, evidence form, arbitration, sanctions, judgment, and interference-specific procedures including priority statements and claim charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean copy of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days of the initiation of the proceeding, each party must file a clean copy of its involved claims and, if a biotechnology material sequence is a limitation, a clean copy of the sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 14-day deadline; applies to all involved claims and biotech sequences when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated copy of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 28 days of the initiation of the proceeding, each party must file an annotated copy of each involved claim indicating (in bold face between braces {}) where each limitation is shown in the drawing or sequence, and for means-plus-function/step-plus-function limitations per 35 U.S.C. 112(6), indicate the specific portions of the specification that describe structure, material, or acts corresponding to each claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotation format required: bold face between braces. Applies both to drawing/sequence limitations and 112(6) limitations; 28-day deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of motions to add or amend a claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to add or amend a claim must include: (1) a clean copy of the claim, (2) a claim chart showing where the disclosure of the patent or application provides written description of the subject matter of the claim, and (3) where applicable, a copy of the claims annotated according to the annotated-copy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim-amendment motions are substantive and must be accompanied by written-description mapping via claim chart; annotated claims per §41.110(b) when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of basis for relief (content and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may require a party to provide a notice stating the relief it requests and the basis for its entitlement to relief. If required, a party will be limited to filing substantive motions consistent with the notice; ambiguities construed against the party. A notice is not evidence except as an admission by a party-opponent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may keep the notice confidential for a limited time. Corrections allowed promptly; late corrections only if entry would serve interests of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim charts required for comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim charts must be used in support of any paper requiring the comparison of a claim to something else (another claim, prior art, or a specification) and must accompany the paper as an appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim charts are not a substitute for appropriate argument and explanation in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of motions and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions are classified as substantive (e.g., to redefine scope, change benefit, or for judgment), responsive (e.g., to amend or add a claim, change inventorship), or miscellaneous (any request other than substantive or responsive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board authorizes the filing of substantive motions consistent with any notice of requested relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for motions
rubrics_metrics.description: The party filing the motion has the burden of proof to establish that it is entitled to the requested relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Movant must make the necessary factual and legal showings in the motion; the Board may require additional showings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for motions, oppositions, and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Each motion must be filed as a separate paper and include: (i) a statement of the precise relief requested, (ii) a statement of material facts, and (iii) a full statement of the reasons for the relief requested, including a detailed explanation of the significance of the evidence and the governing law, rules, and precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where other rules ordinarily govern the relief sought, the motion must include any showings required under those rules in addition to these requirements. The Board may order additional showings or explanations as a condition for filing a motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of material facts format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each material fact shall be set forth as a separate numbered sentence with specific citations to the portions of the record that support the fact. The Board may require that the statement of material facts be submitted as a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This format facilitates pinpointing factual disputes; failure to follow may lead to facts being deemed admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions and replies must identify disputed material facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions and replies must comply with the content requirements for motions and must include a statement identifying material facts in dispute; any material fact not specifically denied shall be considered admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply may only respond to arguments raised in the corresponding opposition; arguments for relief must be made in the motion itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default filing times for motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Default times: an opposition is due 30 days after service of the motion; a reply is due 30 days after service of the opposition; a responsive motion is due 30 days after service of the motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may set a different schedule; these are default unless the Board orders otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous motion pre-filing consultation and authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: If no time for filing a specific miscellaneous motion is provided, the opposing party must be consulted prior to filing; if an opposing party plans to oppose, the movant may not file without Board authorization, ordinarily obtained through a telephone conference including the Board and every other party. Delay in seeking relief may justify denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition to a miscellaneous motion may not be filed without authorization; default times: opposition due five business days after service and reply due three business days after service of the opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit filing with first citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exhibit must be filed and served with the first paper in which it is cited except as the Board may otherwise order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of exhibits prevents later admissibility issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument request and specification of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request an oral argument on an issue raised in a paper within five business days of the filing of the paper. The request must be filed as a separate paper and must specify the issues to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late or non-specific requests risk denial; separate-paper requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required for panel oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: If an oral argument is set for a panel, the movant on any issue to be argued must provide three working copies of the motion, the opposition, and the reply. Each party is responsible for providing three working copies of its exhibits relating to the motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure multiple working copies are prepared and exhibits are similarly duplicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for oral argument is granted, each party will have a total of 20 minutes to present its arguments, including any time for rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time is total per party for the issue; plan presentation concisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrative exhibits timing for oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrative exhibits must be served at least five business days before the oral argument and filed no later than the time of the oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late demonstratives may be excluded; serve early to allow opposition time to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcription at oral arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board encourages the use of a transcription service at oral arguments; if used, the Board must be notified in advance and a transcript must be filed promptly after the oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify Board early to ensure facilities; file transcript promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on motions: powers and order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may take up motions in any order, grant, deny, or dismiss any motion, and take other action appropriate to secure the just, speedy, and inexpensive determination of the proceeding; decisions may defer action on issues until later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board discretion aims at case management and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory decisions and panel governance
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision on motions without a judgment is not final for judicial review; a panel decision on an issue will govern further proceedings in the contested case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel decisions are binding for further proceedings; interlocutory nature limits immediate judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing of motion decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rehearing of a decision on a motion must be filed within fourteen days of the decision; filing does not toll times for taking action. The burden of showing a decision should be modified lies with the party attacking the decision, and the request must specifically identify matters misapprehended or overlooked and where previously addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions/replies to rehearing require Board authorization; panel rehearing of procedural decision reviews for abuse of discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration authorization conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will not authorize arbitration unless: (1) it is to be conducted according to Title 9 U.S.C.; (2) the parties notify the Board in writing of their intention to arbitrate; (3) the agreement is in writing, specifies issues, names an arbitrator or provides a selection date within 30 days, and provides that the arbitrator's award is binding and judgment can be entered by the Board; (4) a copy of the agreement is filed within 20 days after execution; and (5) the arbitration is completed within the time the Board sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are solely responsible for arbitrator selection and conduct; Board will not consider an award unless binding, in writing, states each issue and disposition, and is filed within 20 days of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment effect within the Office (estoppel and finality)
rubrics_metrics.description: A judgment disposes of all issues that were, or by motion could have properly been, raised and decided. A losing party who could have moved for relief but did not may not take inconsistent action in the Office; adverse judgment against a claim is a final action requiring no further Office action to dispose of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judgment has preclusive effect within USPTO proceedings; exceptions exist for issues where party was awarded a favorable judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for adverse judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request judgment against itself at any time; actions construed to be such a request include abandonment of involved application, cancellation/disclaimer of a claim, concession of priority or unpatentability, or abandonment of the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may voluntarily obtain adverse judgment by clear actions that remove involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations to examiner following judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The judgment may include a recommendation for further action by the examiner or Director; if the Board recommends rejection of a claim of an involved application, the examiner must enter and maintain the recommended rejection unless an amendment or showing of facts not previously of record is filed which overcomes the recommended rejection in the examiner's opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners generally follow Board recommendations unless new, overcoming evidence or amendment is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing of judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with a judgment may file a request for rehearing within 30 calendar days of the entry of the judgment. The request must specifically identify all matters believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked and where previously addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 30-day deadline; must point to specific prior briefing/record locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions: grounds for and available remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may impose sanctions against a party for misconduct, including frivolous or unreasonable litigation positions, advancing misleading or frivolous requests for relief or argument, or engaging in dilatory tactics. Sanctions may include orders holding facts established, expunging or precluding filing of a paper, precluding presentation or contesting of issues, precluding discovery, excluding evidence, awarding compensatory expenses (including attorney fees), requiring terminal disclaimer of patent term, or entering judgment in the contested case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions are broad and may be tailored to remedy the misconduct and secure efficient proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery is limited and controlled
rubrics_metrics.description: A party is not entitled to discovery except as authorized in this subpart; parties may agree to discovery among themselves at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery is exceptional and must be authorized; self-agreement between parties can expand discovery without Board order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic discovery obligations (21 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 21 days of a request by an opposing party, a party must serve a legible copy of every requested patent, patent application, literature reference, and test standard mentioned in the specification of the party's involved patent or application, or application upon which the party will rely for benefit, and if not in English, a translation if available, and must file with the Board a notice (without copies) of service of the requested materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt service of these materials is mandatory; translations required when available; failure may affect admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional discovery standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request additional discovery, but the requesting party must show that such additional discovery is in the interests of justice. The Board may specify conditions for additional discovery and when appropriate allow production during cross-examination or authorized testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher threshold than ordinary civil discovery; must justify necessity and relevance to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility requires compliance with subpart rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that is not taken, sought, or filed in accordance with this subpart shall not be admissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural compliance is a precondition to admissibility of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and modification of Federal Rules of Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided in this subpart, the Federal Rules of Evidence shall apply to contested cases; portions relating to criminal proceedings, juries, and other non-relevant matters do not apply. Terminology in the Rules is modified for Board context (e.g., 'Judge' means the Board; 'trial' means contested case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the Federal Rules with the provided term substitutions; Board may consider non-FRE material for foreign law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office records admissibility without certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification is not necessary as a condition to admissibility when the evidence to be submitted is a record of the Office to which all parties have access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records of the Office are presumptively admissible without additional certification formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of evidence and exhibit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence consists of affidavits, transcripts of depositions, documents, and things. All evidence must be submitted in the form of an exhibit and must conform with requirements for papers in §41.106 and the specific exhibit rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits must meet labeling, numbering, and formatting requirements; failure to do so can affect admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non-English documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party relies on or is required to produce a document in a language other than English, a translation into English and an affidavit attesting to the accuracy of the translation must be filed with the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations must be accompanied by an accuracy affidavit to be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit labeling and page-numbering format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exhibit must have an exhibit label with a unique number in a range assigned by the Board, the names of the parties, and the proceeding number in a specific format (example given). When an exhibit is a paper, each page must be uniquely numbered in sequence and the exhibit label affixed to the lower right corner of the first page (or a duplicate first page if affixing would obscure information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict labeling and numbering maintain clarity and traceability of exhibits across the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit list maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must maintain an exhibit list with the exhibit number and a brief description of each exhibit. If the exhibit is not filed, the exhibit list should note that fact. The Board may require filing a current exhibit list prior to acting on a motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep exhibit lists updated; Board may demand current list before rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to deposition and other evidence timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections to deposition evidence must be made during the deposition; for other evidence, any objection must be filed within five business days of service of the evidence and must identify the grounds with sufficient particularity to allow correction in the form of supplemental evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely object may waive the objection; deposition objections handled on the record during the deposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental evidence in response to objections
rubrics_metrics.description: The party relying on evidence to which an objection is timely filed may respond by filing supplemental evidence within ten business days of service of the objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental filing is permitted to cure identified deficiencies; timing is strict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to exclude requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A miscellaneous motion to exclude evidence must be filed to preserve any objection. The motion must identify the objections in the record in order and must explain the objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use miscellaneous motion to exclude as the procedural vehicle to resolve admissibility disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion in limine for ruling on admissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may file a miscellaneous motion in limine for a ruling on the admissibility of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motion in limine can obtain pretrial/adjudicative rulings on evidence admissibility to avoid surprises at hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and content for motions to compel testimony/production
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking to compel testimony or production must file a miscellaneous motion for authorization, describing the general relevance of the testimony/document/thing and: (1) for testimony, identify the witness by name or title; (2) for production, describe the general nature of the document or thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to compel must show relevance and identify targets specifically; authorization is required before compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional requirements for foreign testimony or production
rubrics_metrics.description: For testimony or production sought outside the U.S., the motion must identify the foreign country and explain why the party believes the witness or document can be compelled there, describe procedures to compel it and an estimated time to obtain it, and demonstrate reasonable efforts were made to secure the witness's or holder's agreement to testify or produce in the U.S., including offering to pay travel/production expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher showing required for foreign process: specifics on procedures, time estimates, and prior good-faith efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and timing for taking testimony (affidavit/deposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct testimony must be submitted in the form of an affidavit except when testimony is compelled under 35 U.S.C. 24, in which case it may be a deposition transcript. Uncompelled direct testimony may be taken at any time; otherwise, testimony may only be taken during times the Board authorizes. Authorized testimony may be taken at any reasonable time/location within the U.S. before a disinterested official authorized to administer oaths; testimony outside the U.S. only as the Board directs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe form requirements distinguishing affidavit vs deposition and secure Board authorization/timing for compelled or foreign testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of deposition content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to taking testimony, parties must agree on time/place; if they cannot agree, the seeking party must initiate a conference with the Board. For direct testimony, at least three business days prior, the party seeking direct testimony must serve a list and copy of each document it intends to rely upon and a list/proffer of reasonable access to any thing other than a document. Notice of deposition must be filed at least two business days before a deposition and must list time/place, witness name/address, exhibits to be relied upon, and a general description of the scope and nature of the testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to promptly move to quash a defective notice may waive objections; schedule depositions carefully and provide required pre-deposition materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition procedures, swearing, and recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Each witness shall be duly sworn by an officer authorized under 35 U.S.C. 23; testimony shall be taken in answer to interrogatories with questions and answers recorded in order by the officer or other disinterested person, unless waived. Exhibits relied upon must be numbered according to the proceeding scheme and served if not previously served. Objections made at the deposition shall be noted on the record and evidence taken subject to ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow formal deposition method; objections on the record preserve issues for later motion to exclude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcripts, witness signature, and officer certification
rubrics_metrics.description: When testimony has been transcribed, the witness shall read and sign (as an affidavit) a transcript unless parties agree otherwise or the witness refuses. The officer must prepare a certified transcript with a certificate stating specific matters (sworn, true record, recorder identity, presence of opponents, place/time, no disqualifying interest, refusal circumstances). The officer must promptly provide copies to all parties and the proponent must file the original exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate contents are prescribed; timely distribution and filing of original transcript essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of deposition objections not made on record
rubrics_metrics.description: Any objection to the content, form, or manner of taking the deposition, including qualifications of the officer, is waived unless made on the record during the deposition and preserved in a timely filed miscellaneous motion to exclude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make objections on the record during the deposition and follow with a motion to exclude to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs for testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as the Board may order or the parties agree in writing, the proponent of the testimony shall bear all costs associated with the testimony, including reasonable costs associated with making the witness available for cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for cost allocation; seek Board order or agreement if cost-shifting is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert testimony disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert testimony that does not disclose the underlying facts or data on which the opinion is based is entitled to little or no weight. Testimony on United States patent law will not be admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure expert testimony includes disclosure of underlying facts/data and avoid offering expert opinions on U.S. patent law as substantive legal conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit requirements for technical tests and data
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party relies on a technical test or data from such a test, the party must provide an affidavit explaining: (1) why the test/data is being used, (2) how the test was performed and data generated, (3) how the data is used to determine a value, (4) how the test is regarded in the relevant art, and (5) any other information necessary for the Board to evaluate the test and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits must permit the Board to assess validity, methodology, relevance, and standing of technical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadest reasonable claim construction in interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: In patent interferences, a claim shall be given its broadest reasonable construction in light of the specification of the application or patent in which it appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply broadest reasonable interpretation standard when construing claims for interference proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference pendency goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent interferences shall be administered such that pendency before the Board is normally no more than two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board manages proceedings to aim for ~2-year pendency as a norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and requirement for counts
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'count' is the Board's description of the interfering subject matter that sets the scope of admissible proofs on priority; where more than one count exists, each count must describe a patentably distinct invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts define the scope of priority contest; ensure counts are patentably distinct when multiple counts are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required to suggest an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant suggesting an interference must: (1) identify the application/patent sought, (2) identify all claims believed to interfere and propose counts and show claim correspondence, (3) provide a claim chart comparing at least one claim of each party corresponding to the count and show why the claims interfere, (4) explain in detail why the applicant will prevail on priority, (5) if claim added/amended to provoke interference provide claim chart showing written description for each claim, and (6) for each constructive reduction to practice for which benefit is sought provide a chart showing where the disclosure provides a constructive reduction to practice within the scope of the interfering subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive showing required; claim charts and priority explanations are central; providing constructive reduction-to-practice charts is necessary when seeking benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner authority to require claim to provoke interference
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may require an applicant to add a claim to provoke an interference; failure to satisfy the requirement within a period (not less than one month) will operate as a concession of priority for the subject matter of the claim. The proposed claim must be patentable to the applicant and drawn to patentable subject matter claimed by another applicant or patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with examiner's directive promptly or risk concession; proposed claim must meet patentability and corresponding-subject-matter criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of showing priority and proffer when evidence unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: A showing of priority is not sufficient unless it would, if unrebutted, support a determination of priority in favor of the party. When testimony or production necessary is not available without authorization, the showing shall include any necessary interrogatory/request and a detailed proffer of expected responses and an explanation of relevance to priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial showing must be strong enough to support a favorable determination absent rebuttal; include detailed proffers when evidence needs Board authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference declaration criteria and notice contents
rubrics_metrics.description: An interference exists if the subject matter of a claim of one party would, if prior art, have anticipated or rendered obvious the subject matter of a claim of the opposing party and vice versa. A notice declaring an interference must identify: (1) the interfering subject matter, (2) the involved applications, patents, and claims, (3) the accorded benefit for each count, and (4) the claims corresponding to each count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration lays out the formal scope and parties/claims/benefits; redeclaration may be used to change prior declaration details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority statement content and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may not submit evidence of its priority beyond its accorded benefit unless it files a priority statement setting forth all bases on which it intends to establish entitlement to judgment on priority. The priority statement must state: (i) date and location of earliest corroborated conception, (ii) date and location of earliest corroborated actual reduction to practice, (iii) earliest corroborated date on which diligence began, and (iv) provide a copy of the earliest document relied on to show conception. If a junior party fails to file a priority statement overcoming a senior party's accorded benefit, judgment shall be entered against the junior party absent good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority statements are detailed and consequential; failure by a junior party to rebut a senior party's benefit can be dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may require listing of intended substantive motions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may require a party to list the motions it intends to file, including sufficient detail to place the Board and the opponent on notice of the precise relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice of intended motions helps case management and allows opponents to prepare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement filing timing and access rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agreement or understanding made in connection with or in contemplation of the termination of an interference must be filed prior to termination of the interference. Untimely filing may be permitted up to six months after termination upon petition and a showing of good cause. Parties may request that the agreement be kept separate from the interference file and such agreements are accessible to others only upon petition and showing of good cause; Government agencies have access on written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File settlement agreements timely; if kept separate, public access is restricted and requires petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment in common-ownership interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the Board issues judgment in, an interference between an application and another application or patent that are commonly owned may be resolved under procedures the Board sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common ownership may affect the Board's handling and potential entry of judgment.
